A [Process-Bigraph](https://github.com/vivarium-collective/process-bigraph) research
workspace for composing cell and tissue models across simulation paradigms. Three lines of
work: (1) run one backend-neutral blueprint on three mechanics substrates — Cellular Potts,
vertex, and center-based — sharing the same field/rule/ODE mechanism, with an optional
per-cell subcellular ODE; (2) compose a particle simulator (Smoldyn) with those tissue
models, confining each cell's molecules to its own moving boundary; (3) the **composition
atlas** — couple several sub-cellular simulators (SBML-ODE, Smoldyn particles, MaBoSS
Boolean) *inside one cell* via a `CoupledCell` adapter, and couple all scales at once in a
dividing tissue whose divisions are decided by each cell's own metabolism→fate chain.

## What's inside

A model is written once as a versioned **blueprint** (YAML: cell types, adhesion, fields,
rules, ODEs). The `blueprint_pipeline` composite compiles it onto one of three
mechanics backends: a Cellular Potts model ([viva-cpm](https://github.com/vivarium-collective/viva-cpm)),
a vertex model ([vivarium-tyssue](https://github.com/vivarium-collective/vivarium-tyssue)) or a
center-based model ([viva-munk](https://github.com/vivarium-collective/viva-munk)). The
field, rule, systemic-ODE and immune-recruitment mechanism is shared and identical;
only the single mechanics node differs. An optional **subcellular layer** (a
[tellurium](https://github.com/vivarium-collective/viva-tellurium) ODE per cell) grows
and divides cells on every backend. The worked example is the Sego 2022 influenza
model (ViralInfectionVTM).

A second composite, `bounded_particles`, composes [Smoldyn](http://www.smoldyn.org/)
with the tissue: each cell is a moving polygon, and a Smoldyn sim runs inside it
(reflective boundary, reversible `A+B⇌C`); when a cell divides, its molecules are
partitioned into the two daughters. The particle engine runs in-process where it has a
binary wheel and otherwise through a subprocess bridge.

- **Blueprint Studio** — edit a blueprint and start `blueprint_pipeline` runs from the
  workbench (`workspace/reports/assets/blueprint_studio.html`). Start here.
- **Two investigations.** `influenza-crossparadigm` — one blueprint on three substrates —
  with five studies: `blueprint-pipeline-fidelity` (contract and t=0 fidelity),
  `cross-paradigm-equivalence` (fate agrees, exact position does not, and the test has power),
  `substrate-behavior-at-scale` (distance to CPM on the large tissue),
  `dose-response-crossparadigm` (sign of the dose response across substrates) and
  `subcellular-layer-grow-divide` (the tellurium layer on all three backends).
  `particle-multicell-composition` — Smoldyn particles bounded by living cells, split on
  division — with the `bounded-particles-{cpm,vertex,munk}` studies.
- [`docs/mechanics.md`](docs/mechanics.md) — how each backend works and how the vertex
  knobs were calibrated to the CPM, including where they still differ.

## Run it locally

    bash scripts/serve.sh            # starts the workbench and opens it
    python3 scripts/lint-workspace.py

First-time setup, authoring skills and troubleshooting are in
[`docs/first-run-agent-guide.md`](docs/first-run-agent-guide.md); a tour of the
workspace is in [`NEXT_STEPS.md`](NEXT_STEPS.md); PR conventions are in
[`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md). The code is in `viva_multicell_blueprint/` (`core.py`'s
`build_core()` registers the processes and composites); research state is under
`workspace/`, with directory locations set by `layout:` in `workspace.yaml`.
Files under `workspace/notes/` and `workspace/references/notes/` are kept by cleanup
sweeps (see `workspace/notes/README.md`).
